::: {.cite-bar .domain-aid-sanctions}
[Supreme Court]{.status .status-case} [453 U.S. 654](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-453/pdf/USREPORTS-453-654.pdf){.cite} [Decided July 2, 1981]{.cite} [Opinion by Justice Rehnquist]{.cite}
:::

**Holding.** Yes. IEEPA authorized nullifying the attachments and transferring the assets. No statute expressly authorized suspending the claims, but Congress's long acquiescence in executive settlement of international claims, and related statutes, supported the President's action.

**Question.** Whether the President, to carry out the Algiers Accords that ended the Iran hostage crisis, could nullify court attachments on Iranian assets, transfer the assets, and suspend Americans' claims against Iran in U.S. courts in favor of an international claims tribunal.

Background reading: [Wikipedia article on Dames & Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dames_%26_Moore_v._Regan) (secondary source).

## Why it matters

The first major test of the [IEEPA](../statutes/ieepa-1977.qmd), and an application of [Jackson's Youngstown framework](../cases/youngstown-1952.qmd) in which congressional acquiescence counted as implied authorization. Executive branch lawyers cite it for the proposition that a consistent practice Congress has known of and not opposed can support presidential action.

## Status

Good law; the Court stressed that its holding was narrow.

## Statutes at issue

- [IEEPA](../statutes/ieepa-1977.qmd){.subj}. Held that IEEPA authorized the President to nullify attachments and order the transfer of Iranian assets.

Studied in [Unit 5: Emergency and economic powers](../study/units/emergencies-sanctions.qmd).
